newsitem.title: CANADA: Westmin's Gibraltar buy seen sound.
newsitem.headline: Westmin's Gibraltar buy seen sound.

text.p: Investment analysts viewed Westmin Resources Ltd's C$307 million proposed takeover on Tuesday of Gibraltar Mines Ltd as a wise long-term move despite initial disappointment among Westmin shareholders.
Westmin, a relatively small base metal miner, announced it and Gibraltar, a copper company, agreed to a deal in which Westmin will pay C$8.85 a share for Gibraltar in cash and stock.
"In the long run, it's a good deal for both companies," said Yorkton Securities analyst Doug Leishman.
Analysts said the deal would ultimately give Westmin a much-needed boost in size, a promising new mine in Chile and a fresh source of earnings.
But some Westmin shareholders reacted negatively to the news because it meant near-term earnings dilution and increased exposure to copper, whose price fell sharply during the summer, analysts said.
Moreover, some shareholders were worried because Gibraltar's prize asset, the Lomas Bayas deposit in Chile, will not be in production for several years, analysts said.

Westmin stock took a beating after the news, falling 1.20 to 6.30 as shareholders reacted to the company's projection of 40 percent earnings dilution in the short run. The stock was the most heavily traded on the Toronto Stock Exchange.
The takeover over the next five years could boost Westmin's copper production to as much as 300 million pounds a year from about 46 million pounds, analysts said.
That troubled some shareholders who were concerned about Westmin's increased exposure to the metal amid turmoil in the copper market. But several analysts viewed it as smart purchase.
"It's a good time to pick up copper assets because they are cheaper," said Leishman.
Added independent Vancouver analyst Eric Zaunscherb: "It gives them (Westmin) critical mass. Westmin comes out the other end a more significant company...There are some positive synergies there."

Westmin president Walter Segsworth said he expected Lomas Bayas to begin full production in 1999 at about 130 million pounds of copper a year. Westmin will boost that to about 195 million pounds around 2001 and sees strong earnings growth from the project.
News of the deal boosted Gibraltar shares 1.30 to 7.60, making it one of the biggest gainers.

Analysts said the deal offered an attractive price for Gibraltar shares and ensured the delayed Lomas Bayas project would be developed. Gibraltar faced obstacles obtaining financing but Westmin said it anticipated no problems. Gibraltar recently lined up a US$140 million debt offering and was seeking US$55 million more in financing.
Gold giant Placer Dome Inc said it would tender its 30.8 percent stake in Gibraltar under the offer. Placer sparked the deal by announcing last week it was seeking a buyer for its stake.
